candidates.name: Main Town Hall
candidates.price: 12 zł adults, 6 zł concessions, tower 5 zł, Tu free
candidates.content: The old city hall (built 1378-1492) has a museum inside showing off a nicely decorated room where the town council once met and some historic exhibits about the history of Gdańsk. There are also impressive photos of the destructio

candidates.name: Artus Court
candidates.price: 26 zł adults, 19 zł concessions, Tu free
candidates.content: Impressive merchants' hall, a symbol of the city's power in the 16th and 17th centuries, served as an exchange and as the seat of St. George and the brotherhoods of rich patricians. Now part of the Gdańsk History Museum.

candidates.name: Uphagen House
candidates.price: 10 zł adults, 5 zł concessions, Tu free
candidates.content: Named after the merchant, Johann Uphagen, who bought this house in 1775. It was destroyed during the war in 1945, but completely rebuilt within ten years. In the 1990s, it was opened to the public. There are temporary exhibitions

candidates.name: European Solidarity Centre
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00-17:00 (closed Tue); Sat - Sun 10:00-18:00; last entry one hour before closing
candidates.content: A centre dedicated to the history of Solidarity, a trade union that became the opposition to the communist government. Among other things35, the building contains a museum and viewpoint at the roof terrace (freely accessible via e

candidates.name: Prison Tower and Torture Chamber
candidates.price: 12 zł for admission to the Amber Museum, +5 zł for the tower
candidates.content: The viewing platform of the tower is open in summer months. This building also houses the Amber Museum.

candidates.name: Oliwa Cathedral
candidates.content: Contains an organ built in the mid-18th century as the largest organ in Europe at that time with slightly fewer than 8,000 pipes. There are daily organ recitals which are generally free (with some exceptions).

candidates.name: Museum of the Second World War
candidates.content: A museum with recreations of World War II realities (Polish street of 1930, a shell-damaged scene with a T-34 tank), in an unusual skewed building.

candidates.name: Westerplatte
candidates.content: Park with many information panels about the first battle of World War II that took place here in September 1939. You can also see disused bunkers and a crumbled command-post, as well as a large monument to those who fought in the

candidates.name: Highland Gate
candidates.content: Also called Upplands Gate. It was built in 1576 as part of the city's fortifications. Once the main entrance to the city where the Polish Kings were officially welcomed.

candidates.name: Crane over the Motława River
candidates.price: 8 zł adults, 5 zł concession, 1 zł children. Last tickets sold 30 min before closing. Tickets available in the museum next door
candidates.hours: Opening hours for Dec and Jan: Tue-Sun 10:00-15:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: The former port crane is one of the most well-known buildings in Gdańsk. It is first mentioned in 1367, but was rebuilt several times since then. During World War II it was partially destroyed again. In 1962 after final reconstruc

candidates.name: Gdańsk Post Office and Museum
candidates.price: 8 zł adults, 5 zł concessions, Mon free
candidates.content: There is a small museum which documents the events that happened on 1 September 1939 at the beginning of World War II. It also contains a small active post office. Even if the museum is closed, the square in front has a great (and

candidates.name: Nowy Port Lighthouse
candidates.content: A 28m high lighthouse built in 1893. It features a time ball which was used to synchronize clocks on ships.

candidates.name: Brzezno pier
candidates.content: A nice white-painted wooden pier. There is a small restaurant and an ice cream parlour.

candidates.name: "Bird Paradise" nature reserve
candidates.content: Nature reserve located on marshy terrain close to the old mouth of Vistula. As name suggests it is a place with lots of birds, for which it is important breeding ground. Many water and wetland birds can be seen in this area. Sever

candidates.name: "Gull Sandbank" nature reserve
candidates.content: Another nature reserve on Sobieszewo located on Vistula mouth where new sandbanks constantly form. Favourite of seagulls and seals which reside on these temporary islands. If you are lucky you may see some of them from a distance

candidates.name: Neptune Fountain
candidates.content: Statue of Neptune, patron of the city, installed in 1549. During World War II, the statue was hidden. In 1954 it was put back to its original location on the Long Market.

candidates.name: St. Mary's Church
candidates.hours: 11–16 Mon to Thu, 11–18 Fri, 10–18 Sat and Sun
candidates.content: One of the largest Gothic churches in Europe and one of the three (almost equal sizes) second largest brick churches in the world. There is space for more than 20,000 people in the church. The church contains a large astronomical

candidates.name: Royal Chapel
candidates.content: Differs from typical Gdańsk architecture.

candidates.name: Sołdek Ship (Museum)
candidates.content: The ship was launched in 1948 as the first Polish ocean-going vessel and used as a coal and ore carrier. It was named after the "shock worker" Stanisław Sołdek. It is part of the National Maritime Museum.

candidates.name: Lechia Gdańsk
candidates.content: The "white & greens" were relegated in 2026 and now play soccer in 1 Liga, the second tier. The stadium (capacity 41,600) also hosts big concerts and other events.

candidates.name: "Cult" Film Festival
candidates.content: Festival of esteemed films taking place in June. There are many indoor and outdoor movie shows and concerts. Until 2017 the festival was organised in Katowice.

candidates.name: Polish Baltic Philharmonic
candidates.content: Major orchestra for symphonic concerts and chamber music.

candidates.name: Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre
candidates.content: Guided tours (in English and Polish) are available.

candidates.name: Wyspa Institute of Art
candidates.content: Art Institute on the shipyard grounds. Exhibitions, concerts, performances. A bookshop, Zła Buka, has a selection of books on art and design.

candidates.name: Jelitkowo beach
candidates.content: The most crowded beach in Gdańsk not far from Oliwa district and close to Sopot. Abundant leisure facilities and many places to get your fish or ice cream.

candidates.name: St. Dominic's Fair
candidates.content: Large fair held since 1260 during mid-July and mid-August every year.

candidates.name: Walk the Mariacka street
candidates.content: Take an evening walk down one of Europe's most picturesque streets.

candidates.name: Brzeźno beach
candidates.content: Another quite crowded beach located bit closer to centre, behind large city park. Contains abundant leisure facilities and a pier (mentioned in See section above).

candidates.name: Stogi beach
candidates.content: Calm and very wide beach to the east of city centre in a forest. A bit harder to access than two above mentioned beaches. Water is very quiet on western side due to breakwater. Good viewpoint of container sea port. Naturist beach

candidates.name: Sobieszewo beach
candidates.content: Located furthest away from the city, it is the least crowded beach in Gdańsk. Generally quiet with relatively few eating spots. Many foot and bike trails are located in nearby forest. Good view of Tricity. On beach edges there are

candidates.name: Brovarnia Gdańska
candidates.content: A mini brewery making their own really good beers in the basement of a hotel in restored 18 century granary. Food also served.

candidates.name: Bar Shpinx
candidates.content: Another bar on the main street.

candidates.name: Loft
candidates.content: Nice late bar/club, no entry charges, free food late on weekends, good music and good young crowd.

candidates.name: Pijalnia Wodki I Piwa
candidates.content: Interesting decor from back in the communist period. Nice atmosphere. Vodka shots and the occasional beer chaser are the norm. On a busy evening this place moves an astonishing amount of vodka. You can buy toasties as a bar snack.

candidates.name: Kaffe Perro Negro
candidates.content: A quiet place a couple of blocks from the main street. Has indoor seating and seating on the footpath in good weather. The building is a typical Gdansk terrace, the interior has quirky and interesting furniture. Some food includin

candidates.name: Pierogarnia Mandu Gdańsk Śródmieście
candidates.content: It serves pierogi (dumplings). Big portions; do not order more than one per person. Because it's cheap and good, it's crowded during busy season and lunch time.

candidates.name: Gdański Bowke
candidates.content: Lots of delicious traditional Polish food. Even though it's in a tourist spot, the quality of the food is truly fine. The tatar tastes amazing with different shades of flavour.

candidates.name: Słony Spichlerz
candidates.content: A nice place to seat outside and see the river. Beautiful food hall with a chilled atmosphere and a great variety of vendors around.

candidates.name: Kafe Delfin
candidates.content: A charming, cozy cafe serving delicious apple pie and coffee. Also try their cheap and tasty bread toasts.

candidates.name: Gdańska
candidates.content: An entertaining place to visit. The rooms are filled with antiques according to the principle less is not more, and the waiters are dressed like in the good old days.

candidates.name: Pyra Bar
candidates.content: The food not only has a nice name, but also tastes great. A large selection, solid portions. A quiet place, a garden on the corner of the street, away from the hustle and bustle of the city, but still close.

candidates.name: Manekin
candidates.content: This place mainly serves pancakes with different type of sources and fillings (and not just sweet ones.) Their potato flour pancakes are recommended. Or try the crepe with chicken, camembert and cranberries.

candidates.name: Montownia Foodhall
candidates.content: As the name suggests, it is a foodhall containing about 18 restaurants; mostly of various world cuisines, with a few bars and cafes and a single eating space. It is located in an old U-Boat assembly plant. Accommodation is also av

candidates.name: Restauracja Filharmonia
candidates.content: "Molecular" cuisine in lovely building with great view on the river. Excellent service, but no vegetarian dishes.

candidates.name: Fellini
candidates.content: High-quality Italian cuisine and top-notch service.

candidates.name: Tygle
candidates.content: Modern Polish cuisine. Mentioned in the Michelin Guide.

candidates.name: Hewelke
candidates.content: Outside the city centre but worth the short trip on public transport. Modern Polish cuisine. Mentioned in the Michelin Guide.

candidates.name: Market Hall
candidates.content: Fresh produce in the basement level.
